title: Maximum independent set in the congested clique
formal: Determine, up to constant factors as \(n\to\infty\), the minimum worst-case round complexity \(T_{\mathrm{MaxIS}}(n)\) for computing an exact maximum independent set of an arbitrary simple undirected graph on \(n\) labelled vertices in the deterministic unicast congested clique defined below. The output is distributed: each processor outputs the membership bit of its own vertex in one common maximum independent set. Local computation and storage have no resource bound, but each local computation must terminate. Only synchronous communication rounds are charged.
definitions: For every integer \(n\ge2\), the vertices and processors have identifiers \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). An input is a simple undirected graph \(G=([n],E)\), represented at processor \(v\) by its \(n\)-bit incident-edge row. Initially each processor knows only this row, its own identifier, \(n\), all identifiers and the common protocol; it has no information about edges not incident to it. The communication network is complete, independently of \(E\). Let \(b(n)=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\). In each round and for each ordered pair of distinct processors, the sender supplies one \(b(n)\)-bit string; shorter payloads must use a fixed padded encoding within that string. Different recipients may receive different strings. All messages for a round depend only on the initial state and messages from earlier rounds, and arrive simultaneously at its end. Local computations are deterministic, with finite descriptions and arbitrary finite local memory; no random coins, advice depending on the input graph, or additional communication channel are available. For fixed \(n\), a protocol may depend on \(n\), but it must work for every labelled graph of that size. All processors must produce their final bits after at most its round bound; their set \(S\) must satisfy both independence, \(\{u,v\}\notin E\) for all distinct \(u,v\in S\), and optimality, \(|S|\ge |I|\) for every independent \(I\subseteq[n]\). Ties between maximum sets are unrestricted, provided the output bits describe one such set. Define \(T_{\mathrm{MaxIS}}(n)\) as the least integer round bound of any such protocol, taking the worst case over all input graphs. There is no promise on density or graph structure. This retains the earlier card’s deterministic, logarithmic-bandwidth specialization of the source’s broader question with bandwidth \(b\).
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous nonnegative asymptotic function \(f(n)\), a computably specified family of correct deterministic protocols, and a complete Lean-checked proof of constants \(c,C>0\) and \(n_0\ge2\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge n_0\), the supplied protocol uses at most \(Cf(n)\) rounds on every input graph, while every correct protocol for that size needs at least \(cf(n)\) rounds on some graph. Thus \(T_{\mathrm{MaxIS}}(n)=\Theta(f(n))\) in precisely the stated model. The upper-bound family must be described by one finite procedure taking \(n\), whose local computation is uncharged. Logarithmically separated bounds, a conditional lower bound alone, approximate solutions, or maximal rather than maximum independent sets are insufficient. This is an asymptotic communication-complexity target; the numerical absolute-error convention does not apply to its big-Theta bounds.
why: Exact independent set separates the cost of learning a global optimum from the cost of computing it once the input is known. The complete communication network removes distances and narrow cuts, yet each link still carries only logarithmically many bits. A tight characterization would identify whether this canonical optimization problem intrinsically requires substantially more information exchange than easier graph tasks in the same network. The circuit connections also make it a meaningful test of the limits of current distributed lower-bound methods.

importance.reason: A canonical exact optimization task testing the communication power of the congested clique. Its relevance extends beyond symmetry breaking, although the chosen deterministic model is one specific frontier.

progress.text: Drucker, Kuhn and Oshman define the unicast and broadcast clique models and prove circuit-simulation connections in Section 2. The result does not determine the exact maximum-independent-set round complexity.
Chechik explicitly poses the maximum-independent-set round-complexity question in Section 5.8 of Dagstuhl Seminar 25191, printed pages 18–19.

Bounded searches through 14 September 2026 did not identify matching bounds for this card’s deterministic logarithmic-bandwidth maximum-set task. This is an individually reviewed formulation, not an exhaustive certification of current openness.

context_blocks.text: Each processor starts with a different overlapping portion of the same graph. A processor may talk directly to any other vertex, including vertices that are nonadjacent in the input. The output nevertheless has to describe a globally optimal set, so individually reasonable local choices need not be compatible.

The elementary general upper bound is \(O(n/\log n)\) rounds for this bandwidth. It uses the fact that local work is unrestricted: centralized NP-hardness does not turn into a round lower bound. This bound provides a scale for the question, without asserting optimality.

Maximum and maximal independent sets impose different requirements. A maximal set merely cannot be enlarged by adding a vertex; it may be much smaller than the largest independent set. The many fast maximal-set algorithms therefore do not supply the requested exact optimization guarantee.

Drucker, Kuhn and Oshman distinguish unicast communication from broadcast and establish connections between unicast protocols and Boolean circuit complexity. Their results explain why superconstant lower bounds for explicit functions in this network are difficult. Those connections are model context, not a tight maximum-independent-set theorem.

Chechik’s 2025 seminar question asks about maximum independent set with incident-edge input and communication to every other player. It leaves bandwidth as a parameter and does not specify a randomness convention. The present card preserves its previously selected deterministic logarithmic-bandwidth question; it does not claim to settle the broader bandwidth tradeoff.

sentences: An exact maximum independent set contains as many pairwise nonadjacent vertices as possible.
Each vertex initially knows its incident edges and can exchange a logarithmic number of bits with every other processor in a round.
The target is the optimal worst-case number of deterministic communication rounds, with local computation uncharged.
A tight bound would measure the information exchange needed for exact graph optimization in a network without distance barriers.
The source leaves bandwidth and randomness broader, while this card preserves its explicit deterministic logarithmic-bandwidth specialization.
